chunks: Goodness to parents is obligatory; if they are polytheists, do not obey them or anyone else in sin, for there is no obedience to the created in disobedience to the Creator.
The Prophets and the Trustees have no sins because they are infallible and purified.
The validity of the two Mutas is obligatory as God revealed them in His Book and the Messenger of God practiced them: the temporary Hajj and the temporary marriage of women.
The inheritance laws are as ordained by God the Blessed and Exalted.

The Aqiqah sacrifice is for the male and female child on the seventh day; the child is named on the seventh day, his head is shaved, and charity equal to the weight of his hair in gold or silver is given.
God does not burden a soul beyond its capacity.
The actions of servants are created by creation of decree, not creation of formation; God is the Creator of all things. They do not say predestination (Jabr) nor total delegation (Tafwid).

God does not take the innocent for the guilty, nor punish children for the sins of fathers, as He said: 'No bearer of burdens bears the burden of another,' and 'Man shall have nothing but what he strives for, and his striving will be seen.'

God may forgive and grant favor, but He does not oppress. He does not command obedience to one He knows misleads, nor choose as Messenger one He knows disbelieves, nor make a proof over creation except an infallible one.

Islam is distinct from Iman; every believer is a Muslim, but not every Muslim is a believer. A thief is not a believer while stealing, nor an adulterer while committing adultery. Those subject to Hadd punishments are Muslims, neither believers nor unbelievers.
God does not put a believer in Hell who was promised Paradise, nor take an unbeliever out of Hell who was promised eternal punishment therein. He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills.
Those subject to Hadd are sinners, neither believers nor unbelievers, and they do not remain in Hell forever, but will be taken out one day.
Intercession is valid for them and for the oppressed if God is pleased with their religion.
The Quran is the Speech of God; it is neither the Creator nor the created.
The world today is a house of Taqiyyah (concealment), it is a house of Islam, not a house of Disbelief nor a house of Faith (in the strict sense).
Enjoining good and forbidding evil is obligatory upon whoever has the ability and does not fear for himself or his companions.

Faith is performing obligations and avoiding major sins. Faith is knowledge of the heart, affirmation by the tongue, and action by the limbs. It includes belief in the punishment of the grave, Munkar and Nakir, resurrection after death, reckoning, the Bridge, and the Balance.
There is no faith in God except with enmity towards the enemies of God.

Takbir for the two Eids is obligatory; for Eid al-Fitr it is said after five prayers from Maghrib on the night of Eid to Asr on the day of Eid, saying: 'God is Great, God is Great, there is no god but God and God is Great, and to Him is praise, God is Great for what He guided us, and praise to God for what He tested us.'

For Eid al-Adha in cities, it is said after ten prayers from Dhuhr on the day of Nahr to Fajr on the third day, and in Mina after fifteen prayers from Dhuhr on the day of Nahr to Fajr on the fourth day.
And added to this Takbir is: 'God is Great for what He has given us from the cattle.'
The puerpera (post-partum woman) does not stay in bleeding more than twenty days unless she purifies earlier; if she does not purify after twenty, she performs Ghusl and acts as a Mustahadha.
Regarding drink: whatever makes much of it intoxicating, its little and much is forbidden.

Every beast with a canine tooth and every bird with a claw, their meat is forbidden. The spleen is forbidden because it is blood. The Jarid, Al-Mar, Al-Tafi, and Al-Zamir are forbidden. Every fish without scales is forbidden to eat.
Eggs with differing ends are eaten, those with equal ends are not. Locusts that can fly on their own are eaten, the Dabba (small locust) is not because it cannot fly on its own.
The slaughter of fish and locusts is catching them.

key_terms.الْمُتْعَتَانِ: The two temporary rites (Hajj and Marriage)

ai.seo_question: What are the Shia jurisprudential rulings on temporary marriage, Aqiqah, and the status of faith versus Islam?
ai.summary: This passage from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Khisal* synthesizes core Shia theological tenets, particularly the doctrine of *'Isma* (infallibility) and the middle ground of *Bayn al-Amayn* (neither absolute predestination nor total free will), while delineating the distinction between Islam (outward submission) and Iman (inner faith). It further establishes practical jurisprudential rulings on family obligations, temporary marriage (*Mut'ah*), and ritual practices like Eid Takbir, grounding them in the Prophetic Sunnah and Quranic evidence. The text reflects the Ja'fari school's emphasis on the purity of the Ahl al-Bayt and the specific legal status of those subject to Hadd punishments as neither fully believing nor disbelieving.
